what_matters.tag_note: Bloom Energy · first full session after its results
what_matters.head: Bloom Energy fell 11.2% on Friday, 2.2× its usual day, even though its third-quarter results beat forecasts and it raised its 2026 revenue forecast.
what_matters.detail: Yahoo Finance's market report put the fall down to cash: free cash flow was about −$181M in the quarter, and the company faces heavier spending on expansion. Volume was about twice its usual level. The shares had already fallen on Thursday, in the AI sell-off, before the results came out.

what_matters.head: This is the week's big run of events. SK Hynix reports on Wednesday morning SGT. The Fed decides early on Thursday SGT, with Alphabet and Microsoft reporting two hours later. Samsung, Amazon, Intel and Sandisk report on Thursday.
what_matters.detail: The Fed is widely expected to hold rates after it raised them by a quarter point to 4.0% in September. Bets on another quarter-point rise in December have grown quickly in recent weeks (Investing.com). Chair Kevin Warsh holds a press conference after the decision.

what_matters.head: US oil rose 3.8% on Friday, 1.3× its usual day, as tension with Iran pushed crude higher, and the 10-year yield went back to 5.0%.
what_matters.detail: Brent rose more than 6% over the week, to its highest weekly close since 2022 (Investing.com). The MT Newswires market close summed up the day as US stocks falling and Treasury yields jumping as Iran tensions sent crude sharply higher.

latest.tape_note: The S&P 500 fell 0.5% on Friday, and the Nasdaq 100 ended the day about flat. The chip fund rose 0.5%, but it was still down 3.1% on the week. The 10-year yield rose 4 basis points to 4.99%. Gold fell 1.3% and is down 4.1% over five days. The US dollar was about flat against the Singapore dollar.

recent.headline: Bloom Energy fell 11.2% on Friday, 2.2× its usual day, even though its third-quarter results beat forecasts and it raised its 2026 revenue forecast.
Chip stocks fell hard on Thursday: the chip fund lost 6.8%, 2.7× its usual day, and the Nasdaq 2.6%, its biggest one-day fall since early June.
Meta's revenue beat its own forecast, but a $9.9B legal charge cut earnings per share to $3.83, against the $5.46 analysts expected. The shares rose 2.1% after hours.
After Tuesday's US close, Super Micro raised its estimate of last quarter's revenue to $18.5–19.5B, from its forecast of $14.5–15.5B, citing demand for AI platforms.
Chip stocks fell for a ninth straight session on Friday. The iShares chip fund lost 4.1% on the day and 16.3% across the nine sessions, and software stocks fell with them.
